query_builder.sql_active: The statement in Code is SQL, which filters cannot show. Adding a filter here starts a field query.

slow_query.title: Slow query
slow_query.detail: The query took {{took_ms}} ms and scanned {{scanned_rows}} rows. Narrow the time range or add more selective filters.

wide_time_range.title: Wide scan window
wide_time_range.detail: This query scanned a large unbounded or multi-week time range. Narrow it to the smallest window that answers the question.

low_selectivity.title: Low selectivity
low_selectivity.detail: The query scanned {{scanned_rows}} rows to return {{returned_rows}}. Add predicates on indexed or partitioned fields to reduce the scan.

select_star.title: Avoid SELECT *
select_star.detail: Projecting all columns reads more data than needed. Select only the columns you use.

missing_filter.title: No filter predicate
missing_filter.detail: A large scan without a WHERE clause reads the whole time window. Add filters to reduce I/O.

missing_limit.title: Add a LIMIT
missing_limit.detail: This query returned {{returned_rows}} rows without a LIMIT. Add one when you only need a sample or the top results.

promql_wide_range.title: Wide range selector
promql_wide_range.detail: This range selector reads many samples per series. Consider a recording rule or a smaller window.

promql_subquery.title: Subquery cost
promql_subquery.detail: Subqueries ([..:..]) recompute the inner query at every step and can be expensive. Use a recording rule for frequently reused work.

promql_regex_matcher.title: Regex label matcher
promql_regex_matcher.detail: Regex matchers (=~ / !~) scan more series than exact matches. Prefer = / != when possible, or anchor the regular expression.
